ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the right side of the figure is a passive network labeled N; before the upper input branch of this network, a resistor element labeled R_neg is connected in series; the lower end is a common wire. The port near the passive network N is labeled Z1(s), while the left port after including the series negative resistor is labeled Z2(s). Reasoning: From the series connection in the figure, one can write Z2(s)=Z1(s)+R_neg. Because R_neg is a negative resistor, R_neg=-|R_neg|. If Z2(s) is a positive real function, it needs to satisfy Re Z2(jω)≥0 for all frequencies, so Re Z1(jω)-|R_neg|≥0, that is |R_neg|≤Re Z1(jω), ∀ω.

method.method_draft: For a test sinusoidal current at frequency ω applied at the Z2 port, use the image to note the current is common through the series negative resistor and network N. The real power absorbed by N is proportional to Re Z1(jω), while the negative resistance contributes negative absorbed power of magnitude |R_neg|.
